correctness.rationale: The primary arXiv:2611.11635v1 p. 2, equations (1)–(4) and Theorem 1.1 do state the given sharp variational reduction and absolute directional inequality for every unit u, and identify the projected-volume constant. Scaling the affine profile removes one endpoint; r=∞ correctly represents the zero left endpoint. Independently integrating by the formula I_j=1/(j+1)+2(r-1)/(j+2)+(r-1)^2/(j+3) gives the displayed F(r). Differentiation yields -3Q/(20 A^2 B^2), with a strictly positive denominator on r>=0. One sign change and Q(0)<0<Q(1) give one positive zero and strictly increasing then decreasing F, including strict comparison to the two endpoint values 3/20 and 1/20. The exact resultant is 1769472000 times the displayed sextic in z. In /workspace/branches/check_centroid.py, polynomial powering and Euclidean GCDs modulo 113 give gcd(f,z^(113^i)-z)=1 for i=2 and 3 (and likewise for Q). This excludes all irreducible factors of degrees 1,2,3, hence proves irreducibility at degree six with unchanged leading degree. For the value sextic the actual remainders for i=2,3 are 13z^5-56z^4+2z^3+z^2+14z-42 and 4z^5+19z^4-23z^3+16z^2-48z+19. The replay also certifies the printed decimal prefixes with rational brackets and exact root counts. For the sharpness polytopes the cross-section volume is 4ε^4 tℓ(t)^2, yielding I2/I1; the bottom and top face densities are constant multiples of ℓ(t)^2 and total order ε^2, whereas lateral and end faces contribute O(ε^3) and O(ε^4). Thus their boundary first-coordinate centroid tends to I1/I0. Width is one, diameter tends to one and the ratio is sharp. Uniqueness is of the normalized affine optimizer only.
